market_news.paragraph: Global equities were broadly weaker in the latest completed round of trading, with 6 of the 24 benchmarks tracked on this page closing higher. In the United States, the S&P 500 rose 0.09 per cent to 7,638.51, the Dow Jones rose 0.33 per cent to 52,943, the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.05 per cent to 26,086 and the Russell 2000 rose 0.42 per cent to 2,932.48. In Europe, the FTSE 100 fell 0.14 per cent to 10,775, the DAX fell 0.32 per cent to 25,888 and the CAC 40 was little changed at 8,301.04. Across Asia, the Nikkei 225 fell 2.85 per cent to 64,326, the Hang Seng fell 0.07 per cent to 25,311, the KOSPI fell 3.99 per cent to 6,562.72, the Shanghai Composite fell 0.97 per cent to 3,941.39, the BSE Sensex fell 0.49 per cent to 76,570 and the Straits Times rose 0.59 per cent to 5,744.11. Elsewhere, the Ibovespa rose 1.31 per cent to 182,070. Locally, the S&P/ASX 200 fell 0.97 per cent to 8,978.40 and the All Ordinaries fell 1.09 per cent to 9,160.30. In digital assets, bitcoin changed hands at $77,287, down 0.77 per cent over the past 24 hours. In currencies, the US dollar bought 1.4003 Australian dollars, up 0.29 per cent against the prior business day's fix. Index levels, exchange rates and commodity prices on this page are captured live at build time from the sources linked in each section; no forward-looking view is offered here.
